lines.text: Every language model you have used writes left to right. One token at a time, each waiting for the last.
That loop is the reason inference is slow, and it is not obvious that you have to do it this way.
A diffusion model does not generate. It denoises. It starts with a block of masked tokens and fills them in.
All masked. Nothing decided. Every slot is a question mark.
Then it predicts every position at once, and unmasks only the ones it is confident about.
One step, six of eight slots. Then the next step works on what is left.
Which means the order is not left to right. It is confidence order.
That is the appeal. A handful of denoising steps instead of hundreds of single-token steps.
And for the hardware it is bigger still. Batched matrix multiplies are what a GPU is good at.
But here is the honest part. The tokens are not equally confident. The easy ones get filled early.
So the speedup depends on how many slots you dare to unmask per step.
Unmask too many and you commit to a bad token, and you cannot take it back.
The order is free. The confidence is not.
